title: Visible moonlight gave no clear change in temperature slopes of frog calling richness in four US samples in 2006-2015
abstract: We tested whether visible moonlight changed the link between survey-night temperature and recorded frog richness. We used 78,707 stops from 7,939 NAAMP runs on 609 routes in the Northeast and Midwest in 2006-2010 and 2011-2015. The outcome counted four fixed species. Run effects removed differences shared by stops on the same night. Site-by-survey-number effects removed fixed seasonal site differences. The change in the 5 C temperature slope with visible moonlight ranged from -0.0065 to +0.0160 detected species per stop. All four 98.75 percent route-cluster intervals included zero. Mixed-moon runs, traffic and time controls, site-specific moon effects, and route-and-year uncertainty gave the same broad conclusion. Only 1,343 runs had both moon reports. Chosen survey nights, cloud and canopy effects, missing reports and mixed calling and hearing processes limit inference. The result does not show that moonlight has no effect. It is not a test of climate trends, true richness or air pollution. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and a retrieval recipe are included.
